title: Case: Account holder writes about collection fees on a business account
context: Fennick & Rowe Bindery ships with Heronwick Arc Logistics on a business account. A per-collection fee began appearing on its card statements in March, first against DL-7546. The account holder is verified.
initial_request: For your file. May statement came. Two more collection fees on it. Sent to Business billing under BR-8592. They have it. Nothing needed from you. Waiting for the 20th.

events.from: Customer care line, Heronwick Arc Logistics
events.to: Quillon Rowntree, accounts, Fennick & Rowe Bindery
events.body: Caller: There's a collection fee on every pickup since the start of March. Nobody told us. We never agreed to it. I found it on the card statement. Agent: I can see the line on the account. I'll get that sorted for you. Caller: Sorted meaning what? Agent: I'll pass it on and it will be sorted.

events.from: Quillon Rowntree, accounts, Fennick & Rowe Bindery
events.body: Collection fee per pickup since 3 March. First one on DL-7546. No notice. Not agreed. Told on 8 April it would be sorted. It has not been. Still being charged.

Fennick & Rowe Bindery report a per-collection fee on their account since 3 March, first on DL-7546, with no notice and no agreement. The care line told them on 8 April it would be sorted and nothing has changed. Please tell me whether this fee is a valid tariff change, what notice was sent to this account and when, and what became of the 8 April undertaking. I have made no promise about the charges.

Review BR-8592 opened. A collection fee was introduced in the tariff revision effective 1 March. We are checking whether the notice was issued to this account and how the 8 April call was logged; it does not appear on the billing record. Decision by 20 May, 17:00 UTC. We will write to the account holder directly and copy you. No credit has been agreed. If further statements arrive before then the account holder can add them to BR-8592 in the Business portal; they do not need to come through the desk.

events.to: Quillon Rowntree, accounts, Fennick & Rowe Bindery
events.body: Your query on the collection fee is under review, reference BR-8592. We will give you a written decision by 20 May, 17:00 UTC. Nothing has been decided yet. You can add documents to BR-8592 here.

events.from: Quillon Rowntree, accounts, Fennick & Rowe Bindery
Quillon Rowntree, accounts, Fennick & Rowe Bindery
events.body: Adding to BR-8592. May card statement, two further collection fees, 6 May and 13 May.

events.to: Quillon Rowntree, accounts, Fennick & Rowe Bindery
events.body: May statement received and added to BR-8592. Both further charges are within the review. Decision date unchanged: 20 May, 17:00 UTC.

events.from: Quillon Rowntree, accounts, Fennick & Rowe Bindery
events.body: For your file. May statement came. Two more collection fees on it. Sent to Business billing under BR-8592. They have it. Nothing needed from you. Waiting for the 20th.

must: Takes no action and sends no message.
Gives the reason: Business billing has review BR-8592 open with a written decision due by 20 May 17:00 UTC, which is not yet due, and will write to the account holder directly.
Records that the May statement is already with Business billing, who acknowledged it on 15 May, and that the account holder says nothing is needed from the desk.
must_not: Tells the account holder the collection fees will be reversed, credited or stopped.
Chases Business billing for the decision before 20 May.
Forwards or re-reports the May statement to Business billing, who already hold and have acknowledged it.
Tells the account holder the fee is a valid tariff change that must be paid.
Sends the account holder an acknowledgement that restates the review status or the 8 April undertaking.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3104: people, organisations and references renamed. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
